title: A first collaboration conversation with STXBP1 Foundation

sentences.text: On behalf of the Glut1 Deficiency Foundation, I invite STXBP1 Foundation to explore a careful, family-focused collaboration.
Both disorders are linked to haploinsufficiency—one working gene copy is not enough—but the STXBP1 explanation is contested because it does not fully explain differences between patients.
The atlas identifies shared developmental delay, seizures and intellectual disability; the STXBP1 symptom links remain unverified by human review.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Our Foundation’s natural history study includes people with SLC2A1-related disorders, while STARR (STXBP1 Clinical Trial Ready) follows people with STXBP1-related disorders over time.
An epilepsy-dyskinesia survey study and the Registry and Natural History of Epilepsy-Dyskinesia Syndromes also list SLC2A1 and STXBP1.
Could we compare study approaches before considering any shared data collection?

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please review both supporting and limiting evidence for the contested STXBP1 mechanism; transferring study designs across disorders remains a hypothesis.
SLC2A1 participates in moving glucose across cell membranes, so we should not assume the disorders have identical biology.

Please check whether paroxysmal lethargy, increased sodium inside cells and spontaneous hemolytic crises also occur in STXBP1-related disorders, rather than treating missing records as proof of absence.
Before proceeding, please also check for additional SLC2A1 patient organisations, registries, trials and research groups.
Send STXBP1 Foundation one focused enquiry asking whether STARR could include SLC2A1-related disorders and what eligibility review would be needed.
What patient organisations, registries, trials and research groups exist for SLC2A1-related disorders beyond those verified here?
We propose checking patient-organisation partner lists, Citizen Health, RARE-X and Simons Searchlight intake lists, trial registries and published research groups directly.
Dear STXBP1 Foundation team,
Could we explore a small natural history collaboration?
Our Foundation has a natural history study for SLC2A1-related disorders.
Would you advise whether STARR could consider including this community?
We would welcome a careful review of similarities and differences before proceeding.
Thank you for considering this conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of Glut1 Deficiency Foundation
